content:
The image shows a soybean stem with a large, elongated brown lesion/canker. Key features:
- Affected part: stem
- Brown, shredded/necrotic cortical tissue on the stem
- The lesion appears dry, brown, and fibrous/rotted
- Green healthy stem tissue visible on either side of the lesion
- No white mycelium visible (rules out White Mold)
- The lesion is elongated along the stem axis

This pattern of stem browning/rotting is consistent with several stem diseases. The elongated brown stem canker with shredded cortical tissue, without cottony mycelium, points toward **Phytophthora** stem rot or **Brown Stem Rot**. 

Brown Stem Rot causes internal browning of the pith and vascular tissue — typically requires cutting the stem to see. Phytophthora stem rot causes a chocolate-brown discoloration of the lower stem, often with a distinct water-soaked to brown lesion that moves up the stem.

The lesion here is clearly on the outer cortex, brown, shredded, and extends along a section of stem. This is highly characteristic of Phytophthora stem rot — a chocolate-brown stem lesion that girdlesthe stem. The shredded/eroded cortex is a hallmark of Phytophthora sojae infection.
